facts.text: Pixel-level similarity asks whether simulated sensor output looks like real output; task-level gap asks whether the detector, tracker and braking logic behave the same on both. Visually convincing output can still fail the task-level test.
facts.quote: Pixel-level similarity asks whether a simulated sensor output looks like the real one; task-level gap asks whether the software that uses it (detector, tracker, braking logic) behaves the same on both

facts.text: Pixel-level or signal-level metrics such as PSNR, SSIM and point-cloud distances judge appearance and structure rather than perception and decision software behavior.
facts.quote: Pixel-level or signal-level metrics (PSNR, SSIM, point-cloud distances) judge appearance and structure.

facts.text: Task-level metrics assess detection rate, false alarms, tracking error, estimated time to collision, trigger distance and whether braking occurred at the right moment.
facts.quote: Task-level metrics judge the behavior of the perception and decision software: detection rate, false alarms, tracking error, estimated time to collision, trigger distance, and finally whether the brake fired at the right moment.

facts.text: A physics-based radar simulator dramatically improved mutual-information and structural-similarity scores, yet a detector trained only on real radar data failed to detect most cars in the simulated images.
